conventions.convention: Finite-channel mutual informations and rates use natural logarithms and nats. Gaussian channel rates use bits per use; Gaussian differential-entropy calculations in nats are divided by ln 2. Both binary examples explicitly convert finite information quantities to bits.

Y1=h11 X1+h21 X2+Z1 and Y2=h12 X1+h22 X2+Z2. INR1 is interference power at receiver 1, and INR2 is interference power at receiver 2. Unit real Gaussian noise gives the rate factor 1/2; unit circular complex Gaussian noise gives factor 1.

Gaussian interference encoders are separate deterministic message-only maps without feedback. Messages are independent and uniform; error is average joint message error, and power is expected average block power under the uniform message law.
Finite strong interference requires both displayed conditional-information inequalities for every product input law, rather than only at a chosen optimizing law.
Relay-only causality gives the source no feedback and the relay only its past observations. Full output feedback gives both encoders the past destination/relay output pair, never current outputs.

Multicast destinations know their own source message. Encoders use only their own message and past local outputs; error is the probability that any required estimate is wrong, and capacity uses achievable-rate closure.

The seven-facet Gaussian Han–Kobayashi region uses a nominal split and permits the explicitly proved auxiliary-removal/rate-moving alternatives. It does not require retaining the nominal private INR after such removal.

Euclidean likelihood-ratio coding assumes AC, the stated square-integrable local and packing log likelihoods, finite cut informations, and the stated cost hypotheses. The finite-alphabet branch uses no choice axiom.
Causally conditioned directed information includes the current side-information symbol Zi; the feedback decomposition uses past Y symbols and has a zero first feedback summand.

load_bearing.statement: For the finite or Euclidean multicast networks and product input/reconstruction laws in the Statement, subject to its likelihood, finiteness, choice and optional cost hypotheses, every nonnegative tuple satisfying r(A∩S)<I(X_A;Y_d,hat Y_Ac|X_Ac,Q)−I(Y_A;hat Y_A|X_[N],Y_d,hat Y_Ac,Q) on every required source-containing cut is achievable by deterministic measurable causal codes. The stated closure, pointwise cost bounds, constant reconstructions and separate feasible all-zero tuple are included.

Assume AC. For standard-Borel U,V,Y,S, I((U,V);Y|S)=I(U;Y|S)+I(V;Y|U,S)=I(V;Y|S)+I(U;Y|V,S), as extended nonnegative equalities. If the conditional law of Y given (U,V,S) depends only on (V,S), then I(U;Y|S)≤I(V;Y|S).

Assume AC. For real or complex finite-second-moment X and independent unit Gaussian noise Z of the specified type, Y=aX+Z satisfies I(X;Y)≤κ ln(1+|a|² Var(X))≤κ ln(1+|a|² E|X|²), where κ=1/2 in the real model and 1 in the complex model. The first bound is attained by the corresponding Gaussian input, including zero variance.

For the complex Gaussian channel and nominal common/private powers in the Statement, every nonnegative pair satisfying the seven displayed individual, sum and weighted facets is achievable with auxiliary removal and rate moving allowed. The original split suffices when both additional individual inequalities hold; otherwise the stated one-common/one-unsplit-user construction applies. Codes satisfy expected average power constraints, and closure includes singleton streams and boundary pairs.

Under AC and the stated independent circular Gaussian noise and average input-variance assumptions, h(√s X^n+Z^n)−h(√t X^n+W^n)≤n log2((1+sP)/(1+tP)) for s≥t≥0. For independent user input vectors, the displayed unconditional and genie-conditioned output entropy bounds hold without independence of coordinates within either vector.

Assume AC. For standard-Borel coordinates with arbitrary input marginal and product conditional channel law P(Y^n|X^n)=∏i Wi(Yi|Xi), I(X^n;Y^n)≤∑i I(Xi;Yi) in the extended nonnegative order; input coordinates need not be independent.

For the real Gaussian multicast network, independent Gaussian inputs and unit-noise reconstructions on any chosen node set give the displayed destination-dependent NNC cut inner region, its closure over the stated choices, and the separate zero tuple. For common positive power P and all nodes quantized, the sufficient cut right side is (1/2) log2 det(I+(P/2)G(A)G(A)^T)−|A|/2.

For a finite DMN, independent multicast source messages, finite Q and the specified conditional product input and local reconstruction laws, the closure of the union of tuples satisfying the displayed NNC inequality for every destination and source-containing separating cut, together with the all-zero tuple, is achievable. Constant reconstructions are permitted.

Under the universal finite strong-interference inequalities, independent input vectors passed through independent channel uses satisfy I(X1^n;Y1^n|X2^n)≤I(X1^n;Y2^n|X2^n) and the reflected user-2 inequality.

For a finite relay channel with relay-only causality and fixed law P_Xr P_X|Xr, every positive R<min{I(X;Yr|Xr),I(X,Xr;Y)} is achievable in nats per use. Zero is always achievable; closure of the union over such laws gives the decode-forward inner bound.

For the real or complex Gaussian interference channel with |h12|≥|h11| and |h21|≥|h22|, capacity is the nonnegative region with Ri≤κ log2(1+SNRi) and R1+R2≤κ min{log2(1+SNR1+INR1),log2(1+SNR2+INR2)}, with κ=1/2 or 1 respectively.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit choice assumptions inherited by standard-Borel conditional laws, general KL and Gaussian probability suppliers.
The value-space hypotheses in the conditional-information and memoryless-vector tensorization lemmas.
Ensuring grouped messages, inputs, observations and conditioning tuples remain standard Borel.
Nonnegativity and the equality criterion in Gaussian maximum entropy, conditional data processing and tensorization.
The positive Gaussian comparison density in the real-vector maximum-entropy proof.
Concentration of likelihood tests and finite-second-moment costs; Gaussian coding proofs also provide explicit variance bounds for their blocklength-dependent codebook-energy averages.
Finite probability, natural-log entropy and KL conventions, and continuity of finite entropy summands in the feedback-capacity maximization.
Orthogonal diagonalization and the ensuing elementary square-root, determinant-order and trace bounds in the Gaussian cut-gap comparison.

seams_checked.note: Checked the prerequisite page and its finite no-feedback DM-MAC definition, code definition and capacity theorem against the finite strong-interference consumer. Both use independent private messages, separate deterministic encoders, average joint error, nats and finite public time sharing with conditional product inputs. The consumer uses the supplier's random-code ensemble at both marginal receivers and explicitly selects one codebook pair through the sum of their ensemble-average errors. The page attributes only this finite MAC interface to the prerequisite; its Gaussian results have local coding suppliers.
